heading.en: Is "is taller than" a fair relation?

hook.en: If Ravi is taller than Anil and Anil is taller than Sita, then Ravi is taller than Sita. But Ravi is never taller than himself. Today we name these patterns.
hook.kn: ರವಿ ಅನಿಲನಿಗಿಂತ ಎತ್ತರ, ಅನಿಲ ಸೀತಾಳಿಗಿಂತ ಎತ್ತರ ಎಂದಾದರೆ ರವಿ ಸೀತಾಳಿಗಿಂತ ಎತ್ತರ. ಆದರೆ ರವಿ ತನಗಿಂತ ತಾನೇ ಎತ್ತರನಲ್ಲ. ಇಂದು ಈ ಮಾದರಿಗಳಿಗೆ ಹೆಸರು ಕೊಡೋಣ.

title.en: Define a relation as a subset of A × A
Test a relation for reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity

say.en: If Ravi is taller than Anil and Anil is taller than Sita, then Ravi is taller than Sita. But Ravi is never taller than himself. Today we name these patterns. In this lesson: Define a relation as a subset of A times A.
Recognise empty and universal relations.
Test a relation for reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity.

body.en: A *relation* $R$ on a set $A$ is any subset of $A \times A$. If $(a, b) \in R$ we say $a$ is related to $b$ and write $a R b$. The empty relation $\phi$ relates no pair; the universal relation $A \times A$ relates every pair. If $n(A) = n$, there are $2^{n^2}$ relations on $A$.
body.kn: ಗಣ A ಮೇಲಿನ ಸಂಬಂಧ R ಎಂದರೆ A × A ಯ ಯಾವುದೇ ಉಪಗಣ. ಶೂನ್ಯ ಸಂಬಂಧ ಯಾವ ಜೋಡಿಯನ್ನೂ ಸಂಬಂಧಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ; ಸಾರ್ವತ್ರಿಕ ಸಂಬಂಧ ಎಲ್ಲ ಜೋಡಿಗಳನ್ನೂ ಸಂಬಂಧಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

points.en: Number of *relations* on A with n elements: 2^(n²)

narration.en: A relation on a set A is just a subset of A cross A. The empty relation relates nothing, the universal relation relates everything, and a set with n elements has 2 to the power n squared relations.
narration.kn: ಗಣ A ಮೇಲಿನ ಸಂಬಂಧ R ಎಂದರೆ A × A ಯ ಯಾವುದೇ ಉಪಗಣ. ಶೂನ್ಯ ಸಂಬಂಧ ಯಾವ ಜೋಡಿಯನ್ನೂ ಸಂಬಂಧಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ; ಸಾರ್ವತ್ರಿಕ ಸಂಬಂಧ ಎಲ್ಲ ಜೋಡಿಗಳನ್ನೂ ಸಂಬಂಧಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: A relation on a set A is just a subset of A cross A. The empty relation relates nothing, the universal relation relates everything, and a set with n elements has 2 to the power n squared relations. Empty relation: R equals phi.
say.kn: ಗಣ A ಮೇಲಿನ ಸಂಬಂಧ R ಎಂದರೆ A times A ಯ ಯಾವುದೇ ಉಪಗಣ. ಶೂನ್ಯ ಸಂಬಂಧ ಯಾವ ಜೋಡಿಯನ್ನೂ ಸಂಬಂಧಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ; ಸಾರ್ವತ್ರಿಕ ಸಂಬಂಧ ಎಲ್ಲ ಜೋಡಿಗಳನ್ನೂ ಸಂಬಂಧಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: Universal relation: R equals A times A.
Number of relations on A with n elements: 2^n squared.

title.en: Relations as dots on the A × A grid

say.en: A relation on A is just a set of ordered pairs from A cross A. With three elements there are nine pairs; each dot is one pair.
Reflexive means every diagonal pair (a, a) is in R. Circle the whole diagonal.
Symmetric means the picture is a mirror image in the diagonal: if (1, 2) is in, so is (2, 1).
Transitive: whenever 1 is related to 2 and 2 is related to 3, then 1 must be related to 3 as well.
Let us count. Out of n squared pairs, the n diagonal pairs are forced in for a reflexive relation; the rest are free.

body.en: A relation $R$ on $A$ is *reflexive* if $(a, a) \in R$ for every $a \in A$; symmetric if $(a, b) \in R$ implies $(b, a) \in R$; transitive if $(a, b) \in R$ and $(b, c) \in R$ together imply $(a, c) \in R$.
body.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ a ಗೆ (a, a) ∈ R ಆದರೆ R ಸ್ವವಾಚಕ (reflexive). (a, b) ∈ R ಆದಾಗ (b, a) ∈ R ಆದರೆ ಸಮಮಿತೀಯ (symmetric). (a, b), (b, c) ∈ R ಆದಾಗ (a, c) ∈ R ಆದರೆ ಸಂಕ್ರಾಮಕ (transitive).

points.en: *Transitive*: a chain a → b → c gives a → c

narration.en: Reflexive means every element is related to itself. Symmetric means every pair can be turned around. Transitive means whenever a is related to b and b to c, a is related to c.
narration.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ a ಗೆ (a, a) ∈ R ಆದರೆ R ಸ್ವವಾಚಕ (reflexive). (a, b) ∈ R ಆದಾಗ (b, a) ∈ R ಆದರೆ ಸಮಮಿತೀಯ (symmetric). (a, b), (b, c) ∈ R ಆದಾಗ (a, c) ∈ R ಆದರೆ ಸಂಕ್ರಾಮಕ (transitive).

say.en: Reflexive means every element is related to itself. Symmetric means every pair can be turned around. Transitive means whenever a is related to b and b to c, a is related to c. Reflexive: every element related to itself.
say.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ a ಗೆ (a, a) in R ಆದರೆ R ಸ್ವವಾಚಕ reflexive. (a, b) in R ಆದಾಗ (b, a) in R ಆದರೆ ಸಮಮಿತೀಯ symmetric. (a, b), (b, c) in R ಆದಾಗ (a, c) in R ಆದರೆ ಸಂಕ್ರಾಮಕ transitive.

say.en: Symmetric: every pair can be reversed.
Transitive: a chain a gives b gives c gives a gives c.

tagline.en: Ordered pairs, A × B, relations as subsets of A × B, and domain, codomain and range.

say.en: Ordered pairs: order matters.
$n(A \times B) = n(A)\,n(B)$.
A relation is a subset of $A \times B$; there are $2^{n(A)n(B)}$ of them.
Range is a subset of the codomain.

problem.en: On A = {1, 2, 3}, let R = {(1, 2), (2, 1)}. Is R reflexive, symmetric, transitive?

steps.en: (1, 1) ∉ R, so R is not reflexive.
The only pairs are (1, 2) and (2, 1), each the reverse of the other, so R is symmetric.
(1, 2) ∈ R and (2, 1) ∈ R, but (1, 1) ∉ R, so R is not transitive.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. On A = {1, 2, 3}, let R = {(1, 2), (2, 1)}. Is R reflexive, symmetric, transitive?

say.en: Let us solve this together. On A = {1, 2, 3}, let R = {(1, 2), (2, 1)}. Is R reflexive, symmetric, transitive?
(1, 1) ∉ R, so R is not reflexive.
The only pairs are (1, 2) and (2, 1), each the reverse of the other, so R is symmetric.
(1, 2) in R and (2, 1) in R, but (1, 1) ∉ R, so R is not transitive.
So the answer is Symmetric only.

problem.en: How many relations can be defined on A = {1, 2, 3}?

steps.en: Every subset of A × A is a relation.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. How many relations can be defined on A = {1, 2, 3}?

say.en: Let us solve this together. How many relations can be defined on A = {1, 2, 3}?
nA times A equals 3 times 3 equals 9.
Every subset of A times A is a relation.
Number of subsets equals 2 to the power 9 equals 512.
So the answer is 512.

body.en: To disprove a property you need only one failing pair. For symmetry look for (a, b) without (b, a); for transitivity look for (a, b), (b, c) without (a, c). Pairs of the form (a, b), (b, a) are the usual traps: they force (a, a).

narration.en: Test with the smallest counter-example. To disprove a property you need only one failing pair. For symmetry look for (a, b) without (b, a); for transitivity look for (a, b), (b, c) without (a, c). Pairs of the form (a, b), (b, a) are the usual traps: they force (a, a).

say.en: Pause and solve this exam pattern question. On the set of all lines in a plane, the relation "L 1 is perpendicular to L 2" is.

No line is perpendicular to itself; if L 1 is perpendicular to L 2 then L 2 is perpendicular to L 1; but L 1 is perpendicular to L 2 and L 2 is perpendicular to L 3 make L 1 parallel to L 3, not perpendicular.

say.en: Let us recall the key ideas. A relation on A is a subset of A times A.
say.kn: ಮುಖ್ಯ ಅಂಶಗಳನ್ನು ನೆನಪಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳೋಣ. A ಮೇಲಿನ ಸಂಬಂಧ ಎಂದರೆ A times A ಯ ಉಪಗಣ.

say.en: Reflexive: (a, a) in R for all a.
say.kn: ಸ್ವವಾಚಕ: ಎಲ್ಲ a ಗೆ (a, a) in R.

say.en: Symmetric: (a, b) in R so (b, a) in R.
say.kn: ಸಮಮಿತೀಯ: (a, b) in R so (b, a) in R.

say.en: Transitive: (a, b), (b, c) in R so (a, c) in R.
